findings.title: Stolen sessions retain authenticated access after password changes
findings.problem: Changing the password now preserves session_secret. An attacker holding a valid pre-change triggarr_session cookie can continue accessing protected routes after the owner changes their password: triggarr/web/middleware.py:144–148 validates only that cookie against the unchanged secret, and triggarr/auth.py permits it until its 30-day expiry. No replacement revocation check exists on this path. This removes the existing compromise-recovery protection and contradicts the session-eviction tests in tests/test_auth_routes.py:604–707.
findings.why_it_matters: Changing the password now preserves session_secret. An attacker holding a valid pre-change triggarr_session cookie can continue accessing protected routes after the owner changes their password.
findings.fix_hint: Restore session-secret rotation alongside the password hash update and reissue the acting user's cookie under the new secret. Verify that another device's pre-change cookie is rejected after the change.

members.title: Password change no longer invalidates other active sessions (session_secret rotation removed)
members.problem: The diff removes the session_secret rotation from change_password, leaving only the password_hash update. Since AuthMiddleware/login validate cookies against auth.session_secret (triggarr/web/routes.py:1357, 1470), and that secret is now left untouched on password change, every cookie signed under the old secret -- including one held by an attacker with a stolen/compromised session -- remains valid for the full 30-day COOKIE_MAX_AGE after the password is changed. This directly undoes commit 0866332 ('fix(auth): rotate session secret on password change to evict other sessions'). The tests added by that fix (tests/test_auth_integration.py:182, tests/test_auth_routes.py:604, plus the re-issue/eviction tests around lines 645-706) still assert the rotated/evicted behavior and are not updated or removed by this diff.
source_window: context={"errors": {"new_password": "Password must be 72 characters or fewer"}},
members.why_it_matters: The whole point of a password-change feature is to let a user lock out anyone else who has their credentials or session. Without secret rotation, an attacker who already has a valid session cookie keeps full access even after the legitimate user changes the password.
members.fix_hint: restore session_secret rotation (generate_session_secret()) in the same model_copy/atomic write as the password hash, and re-issue the acting user's cookie under the new secret as before (mirroring the still-present /reset/confirm flow at triggarr/web/routes.py:1937-2006), so other sessions are evicted while the acting session survives.

members.title: Password change no longer rotates session_secret, so a stolen session cookie stays valid after the password is changed
members.problem: The diff deletes the rotation of `session_secret` from change_password. Sessions are stateless itsdangerous cookies (validate_session at triggarr/web/middleware.py:146, max_age COOKIE_MAX_AGE = 30 days at triggarr/auth.py:10). Rotating the secret was the only way to revoke them. There is no server-side session store and I found no other code that does the same job; the only other rotation is in the reset-confirm flow at routes.py:1941, which is a different path. So after this change, a cookie an attacker stole before the password change keeps passing middleware step 4 for up to 30 days.

members.why_it_matters: Changing the password is the main way a user locks out a compromised session. This diff silently removes that guarantee, and nothing in the UI or logs tells the user the other sessions are still logged in.
members.fix_hint: Restore generate_session_secret() rotation in the model_copy update and re-issue the acting user's cookie signed with the new secret (mirror the reset-confirm flow at routes.py:1941-2009).

members.title: change_password reverts the session-secret-rotation security fix, breaking its documented mirror with reset_confirm_post
members.problem: Root CLAUDE.md: "Everything else — style, structure, architecture — yields to the existing codebase's conventions: before introducing a new pattern, check how the same problem is solved elsewhere in the repo and follow that." This diff deletes the session_secret rotation, cookie re-issue, and logger.info call from change_password, which were added deliberately in commit 0866332 specifically to close an account-takeover gap. The sibling handler reset_confirm_post (triggarr/web/routes.py:1846-2012) still performs this exact rotation and its docstring/inline comments explicitly describe themselves as mirroring change_password. This also violates the project CLAUDE.md's Deep Code Review Convention item 2, "Correctness: All tests pass (`pytest tests/ -x`)": tests/test_auth_integration.py:182 and tests/test_auth_routes.py:604 assert the rotation/eviction behavior this diff removes, so they will now fail.
source_window: context={"errors": {"new_password": "Password must be 72 characters or fewer"}},
members.why_it_matters: Without rotation, a stolen or compromised session cookie survives a password change for the full 30-day COOKIE_MAX_AGE, reopening precisely the account-takeover scenario commit 0866332 was written to close. It also leaves reset_confirm_post's in-code documentation lying about parity with change_password, and will cause two existing regression tests to fail on the next CI run.
members.fix_hint: Restore the deleted block from commit 0866332: regenerate session_secret alongside password_hash in the same model_copy/atomic write, re-issue the acting session's cookie under the new secret (mirroring login_post), and keep the logger.info call.

members.title: Password change no longer rotates session_secret, so sessions stolen before the change stay valid for 30 days
members.problem: The diff removes the generate_session_secret() rotation from change_password. Now only password_hash is updated. Session cookies are stateless itsdangerous signatures over the username. triggarr/auth.py:113 checks only the signature and COOKIE_MAX_AGE (30 days), and middleware.py:146 validates against auth.session_secret. So every cookie issued before the password change, including one on a compromised device, still validates for up to 30 days. I found nothing else that does the same job: no session store and no password-version claim in the cookie. The reset flow at routes.py:1941 still rotates the secret, so change-password is now the only credential change that leaves old sessions alive.

members.why_it_matters: The usual reason to change a password is a suspected compromise. Without rotation, an attacker who has a session cookie keeps full access after the change.
members.fix_hint: restore session_secret rotation in the model_copy update (same as the reset flow at routes.py:1941) and re-issue the acting user's cookie

members.title: change_password no longer follows the credential-change pattern that reset_confirm_post documents as its mirror
members.problem: The diff removes session_secret rotation and the acting-user cookie re-issue from change_password, so it now only updates password_hash. Its sibling reset_confirm_post (routes.py:1846-2010) still rotates session_secret (generate_session_secret at ~1941), re-signs the acting cookie under the new secret (~2005) and says in its docstring that it is the 'apply path mirroring change_password (D-08..D-13)' with 'rotates session_secret (invalidates all pre-reset cookies — D-12)'. The two credential-change paths now disagree on whether existing sessions survive.

members.why_it_matters: A user who changes their password because a session may be compromised keeps every other session logged in. A password reset still logs them out, so the same intent gets two different security outcomes, and the reset docstring now gives a wrong description of change_password.
members.fix_hint: restore generate_session_secret rotation plus sign_session cookie re-issue in change_password, matching reset_confirm_post; otherwise update the D-12 docstring and decision record to say the two paths now differ on purpose

members.title: Existing tests that assert rotation, cookie re-issue and eviction will fail, which blocks the test gate
members.problem: Several tests check the behavior this diff removes. tests/test_auth_routes.py:604 checks that the secret rotates and is persisted, :641 that the acting user's cookie is re-issued, and :677 that another device's session is evicted. tests/test_auth_integration.py:182 expects the pre-change cookie to get a 302 redirect to /login.
